title: Impact of preoperative and postoperative modern guideline-directed medical therapy on survival following coronary artery bypass grafting.
authors: Magruder JT; Kim SA; Helmers M; Morris CD; Damle S; Brown WM; Thourani VH
agent_eligibility_evidence: Elective isolated CABG adults (n=4,307); GDMT classes (beta blocker, ACE/ARB/ARNI, SGLT2, MRA) identified pre- and postoperatively; discharge SGLT2 associated with lower mortality (HR 0.39). Preoperative GDMT noted but no protective association reported; unclear if preop SGLT2 specifically analyzed.
agent_rationale: Adult CABG cohort with GDMT classes including SGLT2 assessed preadmission (within 2 weeks) and at discharge; comparator implicitly present. Abstract reports strongest association for postoperative SGLT2 at discharge with reduced mortality. Ambiguity remains whether “postoperative at discharge” qualifies as perioperative exposure per protocol and whether preoperative SGLT2 effects were analyzed separately. Focus is on long-term survival rather than perioperative outcomes. Full text needed to confirm exposure timing/details and comparator structure.

title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use and outcomes after surgical aortic valve replacement.
authors: Jacquemyn X; Hasan I; Ogami T; Serna-Gallegos D; Bonatti J; Abdullah M; Chu D; Kaczorowski DJ; Sultan I
journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
agent_eligibility_evidence: Methods/Study design and Eligibility criteria sections: patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI; randomisation performed after TAVI with empagliflozin initiated 4 weeks post-TAVI. No surgical AVR or other open cardiac surgery population included.
agent_rationale: The attached full-text describes a randomized, open-label trial exclusively in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), not open cardiac surgery.

title: Metabolic acidosis in patients with diabetes 2 undergoing cardiac surgery: The impact of SGLT2 inhibitor use: a retrospective cohort study.

agent_rationale: Observational cohort of adults with type 2 diabetes undergoing cardiac surgery comparing preoperative/perioperative SGLT2 inhibitor users vs controls and assessing postoperative acid–base outcomes.

title: Postcardiac Surgery Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Patients on Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors.
authors: Auerbach JS; Gershengorn HB; Aljure OD; Lamelas J; Patel SS; Ferreira TD; Gonzalez LA; Cabrera JL
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

agent_rationale: Retrospective cohort of adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery comparing preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor users versus non-users with reported postoperative outcomes (eDKA, mortality, infection, ICU and hospital LOS). Meets population, exposure, comparator, and outcome criteria.

title: Sodium-glucose cotransport-2 inhibitor induced ketoacidosis following coronary artery bypass surgery: implications for management.
authors: McCann M; O'Brien A; Larbalestier R; Davis T
publication_type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't
agent_eligibility_evidence: "In a retrospective study of patients with T2D undergoing cardiac surgery at our institution, DKA occurred in 15.3% of patients taking SGLT2i at the time of surgery, compared with 0.47% of non-SGLT2i-treated patients. Intravenous insulin in the first 24 h after surgery was associated with a significantly lower risk of DKA in SGLT2i patients."
agent_rationale: Abstract describes a retrospective study of adult patients with type 2 diabetes undergoing cardiac surgery (CABG focus) comparing those taking SGLT2 inhibitors at the time of surgery vs non-SGLT2i patients, reporting postoperative DKA and effect of IV insulin—meeting population, exposure, comparator, and outcome criteria.
